problem: ObjectNav methods focus on hand-crafted scene representations and ignore perception bias in visual observations: spurious co-occurrence associations from domestic semantic distributions, and semantic conflicts from dynamic viewpoint changes in 2D features.
motivation: Biased visual perception limits the generalization of navigation policies in novel environments. Removing confounding in multi-object features and injecting 3D geometry priors into 2D representations should give unbiased embodied perception.
key_idea: Learn unbiased embodied visual representations by combining causal backdoor-adjustment over multi-object features (Unbiased Causal R-CNN with BICA) with cross-modality 2D-3D alignment using Geometric Consistency (GeoCon), and plug them into a modular Causal-ObjectNav.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims the two biases (spurious association and dynamic-view bias) are separable and each addressed by a dedicated module: causal adjustment for the former and 3D-geometry alignment for the latter.
method: Unbiased Causal R-CNN: a detection framework with explicit assumptions about confounders for multi-object features.
BICA (Backdoor Intervention Causal Adjustment): a module that removes spurious association bias via backdoor adjustment during navigation.
GeoCon cross-modality alignment: encodes 3D geometry priors into 2D representations through Geometric Consistency to counter dynamic-view bias.
Causal-ObjectNav: a modular ObjectNav framework using UEVR, with a corner-based scene exploration module and a target object discrimination module.
